misleading_risk: As written, the proposal has three risks. (1) "'Experimental in napari' ... else 'Soon'" is a silent fallback. A host plugin whose project file says Available or Install from GitHub would be labelled "Soon", which is false, and AGENTS.md forbids such defaults. The mapping must be a closed dict over the four project-schema statuses with no else branch. (2) "Intel Macs: not supported by the author" is inferred from omission in a positive `platforms` list. An author who only listed what they tested would be quoted as saying more than they wrote. The literal wording "not in the author's list of supported systems" is safe. (3) "Experimental in napari" is the host plugin's status, not a test of that app in that host, so it must not read as a per-app verification. The wording is hedged enough; the app's own `hosts` entry stays an author claim. Printing the architecture is low risk: "64-bit Intel/AMD (x86_64)" is read from the release file name, so it describes the file and does not say ARM is unsupported. Two things must not be added: any generic RAM, disk or GPU minimum (no author wrote one, so it would be invented), and any "confirm or remove" demand on VLab4Mic's napari/Fiji claim (the claim is true, see evidence).
refined_proposal:
Build three small things, drop the rest.

1. Declared platforms (fixes the wrong-installer problem on 3 of 6 apps).
- Add an optional manifest field `platforms` to schema/labconstrictor-app.schema.json: unique array, minItems 1, enum windows-x86_64, macos-arm64, macos-x86_64, linux-x86_64, described as "the systems you support".
- Put the logic in a new module scripts/lcsite/platforms.py (about 25 lines, three functions): the author's list or None, whether an asset is listed, and the note text.
- In os_tile, an asset the author did not list is not a button. It becomes the line "Intel Mac: not in the author's list of supported systems." This keeps the "never hidden" rule at pages_apps.py:63.
- In downloads_table, the System cell carries the same words for that row.
- When `platforms` is absent, keep today's tiles and add one Details row, "Supported systems: not stated by the author". Do NOT add a build WARNING: the field is optional, and 3 of 6 apps would open a scheduled-build issue every day.
- The site never reads README prose. The three maintainers add the field in their own repos by PR: GuessTheCondition, LabConstrictor-Playground and CellMigrationLab/LabConstrictor-VLab4Mic, all three with macos-arm64, windows-x86_64 and linux-x86_64. VLab4Mic's README must also be fixed, because it contradicts itself.
- Add the line to the example manifest in content/submit.md. Run `python scripts/check_site.py && python scripts/check_design.py` and update AGENTS.md.

2. Static architecture on Windows and Linux tiles.
- Add a closed dict ARCH_NAMES, {"x86_64": "64-bit Intel/AMD (x86_64)", "arm64": "Apple Silicon"}, with a KeyError on an unknown value.
- Print it in the tile text from assets[].arch, for example "Installer for 64-bit Intel/AMD (x86_64)".
- Remove the runtime override at lc.js:46, or make it append. It already replaces the tile's last `.lc-small` paragraph, which for ARM Chromium visitors is the Windows "More info, then Run anyway" hint, so that hint is lost. The static text makes the override redundant, so this is net code removal and it works without JavaScript.

3. One host label function.
- Add `hosts.status(key)` and `hosts.label(key)`. They read the plugin's own docs/labconstrictor-project.yaml (already fetched into build/sources for the Ecosystem page, via `projects.load_project(hosts[key]["plugin"])`).
- Use a closed dict: Experimental -> "Experimental in {host}"; Available -> "Works in {host}"; Install from GitHub -> "In {host} (install from GitHub)"; Deprecated -> "{host} plugin no longer maintained". Fail with a clear message on anything else.
- Use `label` in cards.host_chip (cards.py:62-65), cards.host_badge (cards.py:68-71) and the Details row (pages_apps.py:147). Rename that row and the App Centre filter label at pages_apps.py:27 from "Works in" to "Programs", because the filter selects apps that declare a program whatever its maturity.
- Update AGENTS.md line 29 and DESIGN.md lines 32 and 49, which cite "Soon in napari". DESIGN.md asks for the change in the same pull request.
- Optional copy edit, not code: data/site.yaml:8 ("Soon, apps can also work inside napari...") and data/hubs.yaml:24 and :68 ("(soon)") say "soon" for plugins that exist and are Experimental. Reword them by hand.

4. Tests, in tests/test_site.py. Each needs the failure case, as AGENTS.md requires.
- An unlisted platform renders the explicit line and no button.
- An absent `platforms` leaves the tiles unchanged and adds the "not stated" row.
- A bad enum value is rejected by the schema.
- An unknown project status raises.
- The header badge and the Details row use the same label string.

Drop from the original proposal:
- The per-build WARNING.
- The hardware/RAM/disk work. No author wrote RAM or disk figures, so the site cannot show any. Free-text needs belong in G1's `limitations`, written by the author.
- "VLab4Mic needs maintainers to confirm or remove napari/Fiji". The claim is true.
evidence:
Verified on the built pages in /home/user/labconstrictor-site/site/ and in the code.

(a) Wrong installer offered: CONFIRMED, and worse than claimed (3 of 6 apps).
- Built /apps/guessthecondition/ and /apps/labconstrictor-playground/ show "Intel 179 MB · .pkg" and list the macOS (Intel) .pkg and .sh in "All downloads".
- /home/user/GuessTheCondition/README.md:49 says "Apple-silicon Macs are supported; Intel Macs are not."
- /home/user/LabConstrictor-Playground/README.md:32 says "Windows, Apple Silicon Mac, Linux; Intel Macs are not supported".
- The auditor missed VLab4Mic. The live README at CellMigrationLab/LabConstrictor-VLab4Mic (via gh api) says "the .pkg for a Mac with an Apple chip (M1 or newer; Intel Macs are not supported)" in the install steps, but its table at line 39 says ".pkg (ARM64 or Intel)". The built /apps/labconstrictor-vlab4mic/ shows the Intel button.
- NucleiSky, CellTracksColab and Demo say nothing against Intel. NucleiSky and Demo state nothing about Mac chips; CellTracksColab says only "installer for Windows, macOS or Linux".
- The template builds Intel for every app (/home/user/LabConstrictor/.github/workflows/release_constructor.yml:93-94, macos-15-intel). It has no opt-out; grep for "intel" found none.
- The manifest has no platform field: schema/labconstrictor-app.schema.json has `hosts` and `distribution` only. The generic install guide (/guides/install/) tells every user "If ... Intel, download the Intel installer".
- Only an author-declared field can fix this, because the site must not parse READMEs. I did not verify whether the Intel installers actually fail, only that the authors say they are unsupported.

(b) Contradictory host claims: CONFIRMED.
- Built GuessTheCondition page header: "Soon in napari", "Soon in Fiji". Details row of the same page: "Works in [napari logo] napari [Fiji logo] Fiji".
- The same split appears on the App Centre cards: chips titled "Soon in napari", filter label "Works in" (pages_apps.py:27).
- Hard-coded at cards.py:62-71. Details row at pages_apps.py:147, works_in at :170.
- The plugin project files in build/sources/CellMigrationLab__{napari-labconstrictor,LabConstrictor-Fiji,LabConstrictor-QuPath}/docs/labconstrictor-project.yaml all say `status: Experimental`.
- The built /guides/napari/ and /guides/fiji/ say "Under heavy construction ... untested and unlikely to be stable. Tested on Linux. Windows and macOS are untested". Fiji needs a Maven build.
- So "Soon" understates (the plugins exist and are installable) and "Works in" overstates. The maturity data already exists in each plugin repo, and `hosts.host_of_plugin` plus `projects.load_project` can supply it.

(c) VLab4Mic has no napari/Fiji text: REFUTED. The auditor read the wrong repository.
- /home/user/LabConstrictor-VLab4Mic is a clone of HenriquesLab/LabConstrictor-VLab4Mic, last commit 2026-06-09, with no labconstrictor-app.yaml.
- The registry (registry/CellMigrationLab__LabConstrictor-VLab4Mic.yaml) tracks the fork CellMigrationLab/LabConstrictor-VLab4Mic. That fork has the manifest with `hosts: [notebook, napari, fiji]`.
- It also has src/vlab4mic_lc_tools/__init__.py and lc_tests/cases.json, and a README section "Use VLab4Mic from Napari and Fiji (experimental)" describing exactly two tools: "Simulate imaging of a virtual sample" and "Compare an image with a reference". The manifest's "Two of its tools also run in Napari and Fiji" is true. The README calls the integration experimental, so on this page "Soon" is also wrong.

(d) Architecture and requirements: PARTLY CONFIRMED.
- The Windows tile reads "Windows installer 290 MB · .exe" and the Linux tile "Linux installer 205 MB · .sh", with no architecture. Every asset is x86_64.
- lc.js:19-46 already shows "Only 64-bit Intel/AMD (x86_64) installers exist; this device looks like ARM" to ARM visitors, but only with JavaScript and a Chromium browser. That line replaces the tile's last `.lc-small` paragraph, which is the Windows "More info, then Run anyway" hint.
- No built app page states RAM, disk or GPU needs (grep of site/: only the Playground summary mentions "GPU").
- No app README states RAM or disk requirements either, so there is nothing author-written for the site to show.

Proportionality: about 60 lines of code in one new small module plus edits to cards.py, pages_apps.py and the schema (all files stay under 300 lines, functions under 30), roughly five tests, and one line in content/submit.md. That is worth it for P0 "downloads and compatibility claims accurate", because the contradiction touches 3 of 6 apps and all 3 host-integrating apps. There are no rule conflicts: the field is optional and author-controlled, and the host maturity comes from the plugin repos' own status files, so there is no second description.
